sources_considered.why: Transparent matched-bond analysis provides an independent measurement and explains the difference between coupons and prospective borrowing costs.
Dated secondary transcription of Treasury data supplies an in-period observation after the official page timed out.
Readable reporting describes risk concerns and the differing treatment of completed assets.

evidence_items.locator: Opening analysis following the October 19 update
evidence_items.explanation: The matched sample’s median issuer spread rose from 334 to about 413 basis points, compared with a one-basis-point move in its broader high-yield comparison. The analysis explains why higher yields indicate more expensive prospective financing while existing fixed coupons remain unchanged.
The reported Treasury yield exceeds 5% immediately before publication; the page also reports 5.09% on October 16. These are in-period observations, unlike later declines.

evidence_items.locator: Section 'Market Divergence: Operational Assets Relatively Resilient'
evidence_items.explanation: The report links credit concerns to execution delays and uncertain returns, but also describes relative resilience for completed facilities. This limits any universal interpretation of the claim.
